title: The Shell That Bounced Back
set_language: Manchester 1909 dark scattering room (Rutherford, Geiger, Marsden, gold foil, green scintillation screen); then empty football stadium pea metaphor. Say 'same 1909 dark scattering set' / 'same empty stadium set'. Never 'same DNA'.
continuity_lock: Explorer once only on stadium pea beat. Readable Rutherford face (big moustache).
explorer_lock: Exactly ONE Explorer plate: stadium pea. On model. Attach Explorer reference. Not in first minute (already past).
forbidden: HARD REJECT: Orbit robot; photoreal; Ken Burns or still push; gore; lava drip / molten bead; underside lamp bulb or shade cup; unfinished flat cards; unfinished Explorer hair; DNA helix; readable text or logos baked into the plate (labels added in edit); twin Explorer; never say 'same DNA' or 'lab DNA' in a Veo prompt. No Explorer except stadium pea plate. No battle/gore.
motion_lock: Real Veo motion; Quality for green scintillation flashes.
quality_note: Quality for green flash / dark-room glow.

plates.vo_land: Manchester, nineteen-oh-nine. Ernest Rutherford has a new kind of bullet: alpha particles, tiny and fast, thrown out by radioactive rocks.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Manchester 1909 dark room. Rutherford (readable face, big moustache) with Geiger and young Marsden at gold foil apparatus. Continuous setup. Silent. No Explorer. HARD REJECT: Orbit, unfinished faces, gore.

plates.vo_land: Picture yourself in that room. The lights are off, and you sit in the dark until your eyes adjust. You look through a microscope at a small screen. Each time a particle hits it, you see a tiny green flash, and you count it.
plates.prompt: Same 1909 dark scattering set. POV / eyepiece; tiny green flashes counted one by one. Continuous flash. Quality clean green. Silent. HARD REJECT: lava, Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Now, if Thomson's pudding is right, every bullet should punch straight through. Almost all of them do.
plates.prompt: Same set. Stream of glowing bullets hits gold foil; almost all pass through. Continuous stream. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: But about one in eight thousand bounces back.
plates.prompt: Same set. One bullet bounces back at a steep angle — surprise. Continuous. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Rutherford said it was as if you fired a huge shell at a piece of tissue paper, and it came back and hit you.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Metaphor image: huge shell vs tissue paper that bounces back (wonder, not war gore). Continuous. Silent. HARD REJECT: battle gore, Orbit, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: Then, in nineteen-eleven, he explains it. Nearly all of an atom's mass is packed into a tiny, positive centre, which he calls the nucleus. The electrons sit far outside it. Everything in between is almost empty.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Cutaway atom: tiny positive centre, electrons far out, empty between. Continuous. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, DNA helix, Explorer.

plates.vo_land: How empty? Imagine you are standing in the middle of a football stadium, holding a pea. If the atom were the whole stadium, the nucleus would be that pea.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Giant empty football stadium; exactly ONE Explorer on the centre spot holding up a pea, looking up at far-away stands. Continuous look-up. Attach Explorer reference. Silent. HARD REJECT: twins, no glasses, Orbit, parked forever without acting.

plates.vo_land: The electrons would be somewhere out past the back row of seats. Everything else, all around you, is nothing at all.
plates.prompt: Same empty stadium set. Camera lifts past empty seats — vast nothing. Continuous. Silent. No Explorer required. HARD REJECT: Orbit, crowd fill.

plates.vo_land: That raised a new question. If every element has its own nucleus, what makes one nucleus different from another? A Dutch lawyer and amateur scientist, Antonius van den Broek, had a bold guess: an element's place in the table might equal the positive charge in its nucleus.
plates.prompt: Animistry premium 3D cartoon. Table place linked to a glowing positive charge in a nucleus — guess, not proof yet. Continuous. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Explorer, DNA helix.

plates.vo_land: It was a brilliant guess, but nobody could measure it. Yet.
plates.prompt: Same idea set. Question hangs; instruments not ready. Continuous soft hold-with-motion. Silent. HARD REJECT: Orbit, Ken Burns only.
